 Why Egor Dëmin, Mikel Brown Jr. have barely seen the floor together for Nets 
 By 
 Brian Lewis 
 Published 
 Oct. 26, 2026, 8:43 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 Egor Dëmin and Mikel Brown Jr. are the foundation of the Nets rebuild. But going into the season’s fourth game, they’ve played just four minutes together.
 The duo’s only action together was a cameo in Cleveland on Saturday. Now, after Brown was rested on the tail end of a back-to-back Sunday, he’s cleared to return — albeit still on a minutes limit — Tuesday in Boston.
 With the Nets dragging a winless 0-3 record into TD Garden, seeing Brown potentially play alongside Dëmin would give fans something to look forward to.
 But the Nets are intent on slow-playing it.
 Brooklyn Nets’ Egor Demin (8) celebrates after scoring during the fourth quarter against the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. The Cavaliers defeated the Nets 125-121. Getty Images 
 Brown’s minutes limit has kept him from starting. But asked if he’d look to get him on the floor alongside Dëmin within those constraints, coach Jordi Fernández suggested that’s something dictated by game flow.

 “We have all this preparation, the coaches do a great job putting all these pages and film,” Fernández said. “But then at the end of the day, you have to react to a lot of things that are not controllable. Would I like to play them together? Yes. But if I’m just thinking about playing them together, I may not do what’s best for the group at the moment.”
 Or what’s best for Brown long-term. The rookie played just 19 games at Louisville, missing the second half of his lone season with a back injury. While a rolled ankle cost him the first three preseason games, it’s more caution over the back injury that had Brown rested Sunday night.
 “Correct. There’s not a new injury,” said Fernández. “We’re required to say … So he’s good. He’s doing great. Then after this game, he’ll be ready to go.”
 Brown and Dëmin were a plus-5 in their four-minute stint together against the Cavs.
